To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have successfully encapsulated Pc into pNIPAM microgel particles, with or without lipid decoration.
the hydrophobic phthalocyanine is encapsulated with poly(N-isopropyacrylamide), and the resulting microspheres are used as drug carriers for hydrophobic drugs to be internalized in HeLa cells.

we encapsulate phthalocyanine into poly(N-isopro-pylacrylamides) and poly(N-isoproylacylamide)/lipid composite microspherical particles, which can be used for the controlled release of phthalocyanines, and for the delivery of phthalocianines to cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the encapsulation of Pc into pNIPAM/lipo composite particles for improving its solubility and preventing its aggregation in water.
the synthesis of poly(N-isopropyacrylamide)(pNIPAM)/lipid composite microspherical particles for encapsulation of hydrophobic phthalocyanines.

the synthesis of a series of poly(N-isopro-pylacrylamides) (polyNIPAMs) with different degrees of cross-linking, and with the use of these polyNIPAMs as microgel particles to encapsulate hydrophobic drugs for the purpose of controlled release and photodynamic therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this work provides new insight into the design and fabrication of thermo-responsive composite microspheres for efficient encapsulation of hydrophobic molecules and their controlled release, which is beneficial for the development of novel nanocarriers in drug delivery, cancer diagnosis and therapy.

this work provides a promising strategy to encapsulate hydrophobic Pc into pNIPAM and pNIPAM/lidid composite microspherical particles to improve its water-solubility and prevent the Pc aggregation in aqueous solution.

the encapsulation of Pc with pNIPAM microgel and/or lipid decoration can efficiently improve the solubility and stability of Pc in aqueous medium, and the thermo-responsive release of Pc can effectively promote the PDT effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel approach for the preparation of thermo-responsive microspheres that can be used for the encapsulation and controlled release of hydrophobic photosensitizers.

hydrophobic Pc can be encapsulated into pNIPAM microgel particles to improve its water-solubility, prevent its aggregation in water medium, and achieve its controlled release in response to the temperature change.
the lipid molecules are incorporated into the polymeric microgel particles to improve the loading efficiency of hydrophobic drug and enhance the drug release.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we successfully synthesized poly(N-isopropyacrylamide)(PNIPAM)-based microgels with phthalocyanine encapsulation and lipid coating.
the lipid molecules can be used as the carrier to encapsulate hydrophobic Pc into pNIPAM microgel particles to improve its water-solubility and prevent its aggregation in aqueous media.

lipid molecules can be used as a carrier for the encapsulation of hydrophobic photosensitizers, and this composite can be further loaded into thermo-responsive microgels to improve their water solubility, prevent aggregation, and achieve thermo-responsive release of drugs.
